An exciting trend and one we expect to continue.”The Claude developer is expected to price its IPO after Wednesday’s market close, with its shares scheduled to debut on the Nasdaq on Thursday.For live updates on US Markets, click here“We expect significant interest in Anthropic options once they list,” said Garrett DeSimone, head quant at OptionMetrics. “The combination of AI-driven enthusiasm and the lottery-like payoff profile typical of IPOs is likely to draw investors immediately. As one of the most concentrated pure-play exposures to AI, the stock is also likely to be highly volatile.”Ophir Gottlieb, chief executive of Capital Market Laboratories, said that demand for Anthropic options could exceed the interest seen in SpaceX contracts earlier this year. He cited the offering’s oversubscription, its rising valuation and sharp divisions among investors over the outlook for AI stocks.“The AI trade is melting down,” Gottlieb added. “Many feel it is overdone, while many others feel it’s the popping of a bubble. Whenever there are such opposing views in a heated market, we get a lot of option positioning.”Also Read: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above target range, according to sourcesOptions give investors the right, but not the obligation, to buy or sell shares at a predetermined price within a specified period. They can provide a less expensive way to gain exposure to a stock and express views on short-term price swings or longer-term performance.Anthropic’s $64 billion IPO has attracted stronger early institutional demand than SpaceX’s offering, with the order book six times oversubscribed last week, Reuters previously reported.Wall Street firms are preparing for what could be a record market debut by introducing products linked to Anthropic shares, hosting client events and distributing promotional merchandise.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. articles.title: Anthropic IPO: AI company's listing on Nasdaq to turn thousands of staff into millionaires
articles.summary: Anthropic’s upcoming IPO is expected to generate thousands of paper millionaires among current and former employees, potentially creating one of Silicon Valley’s biggest employee wealth windfalls.The Claude maker’s IPO is expected to open on Nasdaq on Thursday at $70-$78 per share, valuing the company at up to $1.4 trillion. Final pricing is expected on Wednesday night.Estimates of employee wealth vary. Hill, a San Francisco-based private-share marketplace, estimates that 598 non-founder employees could hold at least $100 million in equity each after the listing. Private-markets research firm Sacra estimates that around 2,800 current and former employees could have at least $1 million in pretax vested equity at a $1.35 trillion valuation.For live updates on US Markets, click hereBoth estimates are model-based and rely on publicly available information. Reuters could not independently verify them.Anthropic disclosed that employees holding stock options had accumulated $119 billion in paper gains as of September 30, based on a weighted average exercise price of $2.91 per share. Around $73 billion of these gains had vested and could be exercised immediately."The idea of equity appreciating to an amount that is life-changing is something that people strive for," Hill CEO Andrew Benson said. "It doesn't get better than this."Early employees stand to gain the most from Anthropic listingEmployees who joined Anthropic in its early years, including those in junior and administrative roles, could see substantial financial gains because their stock options carried significantly lower exercise prices.Options granted through 2023 and still outstanding at the end of that year had an average exercise price of just 52 cents per share."Early employees who started in a very junior role should have actually a better financial outcome than somebody who joined in a very senior role right before the IPO," Benson said, referring to Anthropic.Non-founder employees will be allowed to sell up to 10% of their holdings on the first trading day, followed by another 35% after the company's fiscal 2026 earnings.Also Read: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller presses for half-point December rate hike as inflation persistsStock awards extended beyond AI talentFounded in 2021, Anthropic expanded its workforce to approximately 5,300 employees by September 30, from around 940 at the end of 2024. Stock-based compensation played a significant role in attracting talent.A May 2024 job advertisement for an administrative business partner offered an annual salary of $140,000-$190,000, while describing equity as "a major component of the total compensation". This highlights how stock awards extended beyond researchers and engineers to administrative and support staff.In 2024, Anthropic granted employees stock options at an average exercise price of $1.30 per share."And as we know from several anecdotes after the SpaceX IPO, this is often enough to help people down the organization chart do quite well in IPO," said Marcelo Ballve, head of research at Sacra.The filing also disclosed that CFO Krishna Rao received 14 million stock options in 2024 at an exercise price of $1.30 each. At the proposed IPO price range, these options could carry approximately $1 billion in gross intrinsic value, before exercise costs and taxes.Ballve noted that equity awards for administrative and entry-level employees are common at venture-backed companies, although some firms reduce upfront grants as they scale. Following its IPO, Anthropic is likely to reserve such grants primarily for recruiting top talent, he added.

articles.title: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller presses for half-point December rate hike as inflation persists
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller called for a more forceful response to persistent inflation, suggesting policymakers should consider raising interest rates by half a percentage point at their December meeting, according to reports.“We have to be a little more aggressive in our rate hikes to try to get inflation down,” Waller said Wednesday in an interview with CNBC.Inflation data from the past three months imply an annualised rate of about 3.5%, Waller said, significantly above the Fed’s 2% target.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe central bank could either raise rates by 50 basis points in December or deliver two quarter-point increases in December and January. However, Waller said the second approach would work only if officials clearly signalled that another hike would follow in January.Without a “credible signal” of further tightening, financial markets would not reflect the full impact of the planned increases, he said.“So in that world, if you’re not going to signal this very clearly to markets,” Waller added, “then you have to go 50 in December to put it in place and get it done.”The Fed left its benchmark rate unchanged last month after increasing it in September for the first time in three years. Minutes from the October meeting are scheduled for release at 2 p.m. Wednesday in Washington.Fed officials have broadly agreed that further tightening will be necessary, but they remain divided over how quickly rates should rise.Also Read: Fed policymakers focused on inflation risks in October, with some seeing need for bigger rate hikeWaller first raised the possibility of a half-point increase on November 10, warning that a larger move might be needed to preserve the central bank’s inflation-fighting credibility.His comments came shortly before data showed consumer prices increased more than expected. Core inflation rose 0.3% from the previous month, reaching the level Waller had identified as strengthening the case for a larger rate increase.Waller’s position is more hawkish than that of several other policymakers. New York Fed President John Williams pushed back against an outsized move on Tuesday, although he acknowledged that the central bank still had work to do to return inflation to its 2% target.“I don’t think the situation calls for dramatic action,” Williams said at an Axios event in New York. He added that the Fed’s approach of taking time to evaluate incoming data had worked well.Interest-rate futures indicate that investors expect quarter-point increases in December and January, followed by another hike by April.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Morgan Stanley help Mahanadi Coalfields mop up Rs 2,295 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Coal India’s wholly owned subsidiary, Mahanadi Coalfields, has raised ₹2,295.24 crore from anchor investors ahead of its Rs 8,981.2-crore initial public offering (IPO), with global financial institutions such as Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley featuring in the allocation alongside domestic institutional investors, including Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).According to the company's stock exchange filing dated November 18, Mahanadi Coalfields has finalised the allocation of 16,87,68,255 equity shares to anchor investors at Rs 136 per share.LIC was the largest individual anchor investor, receiving 4,17,64,690 equity shares worth Rs 567.99 crore.Domestic mutual funds accounted for the largest share of the anchor allocation, receiving 8,95,22,070 equity shares, representing 53.04% of the total allocation. A total of 11 domestic mutual funds participated through 29 schemes.The participating fund houses included Nippon India, WhiteOak Capital, Tata Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential, Aditya Birla Sun Life, Motilal Oswal, Edelweiss, Axis and Baroda BNP Paribas. Invesco India also participated through its Contra Fund.The anchor book also featured several prominent international financial institutions and investment vehicles.Goldman Sachs Bank Europe SE was allocated 7,35,240 shares worth approximately Rs 10 crore, while Citigroup Global Markets Mauritius Private Limited received 3,67,648 shares worth approximately Rs 5 crore.Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore Pte was allocated 36,76,420 shares worth approximately Rs 50 crore. French banking group Société Générale also featured in the list, receiving 40,44,068 shares worth approximately Rs 55 crore.Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), through its Monsoon investment vehicle, received 17,64,730 shares worth approximately Rs 24 crore.Other overseas-linked investment vehicles named in the filing included Ashoka India Equity Investment Trust, Ashoka WhiteOak ICAV, Integrated Core Strategies Asia Pte Ltd, Venus Investments VCC and Abundantia Capital VCC.Meanwhile, five life insurance companies and pension funds were allocated 4,45,03,615 equity shares, accounting for 26.37% of the total anchor investor allocation.Apart from LIC, the participating insurance companies and pension funds included Bajaj Life Insurance, Edelweiss Life Insurance, Canara HSBC Life Insurance and NPS Trust through UTI Pension Fund's Atal Pension Yojana scheme.Mahanadi Coalfields IPO detailsMahanadi Coalfields IPO is set to open for subscription on November 19, 2026, and will remain open until November 23, giving investors a three-day bidding window.The book-built issue comprises 66.18 crore equity shares and is entirely an offer for sale (OFS) by the existing shareholder, Coal India Limited. Consequently, Mahanadi Coalfields will not receive any proceeds from the public issue, with the entire proceeds, after applicable offer-related expenses and taxes, going to the selling shareholder.The company has fixed the IPO price band at Rs 129-136 per equity share, with a face value of Rs 2 per share. The floor price represents 64.50 times the face value, while the upper end of the price band is 68 times the face value.Investors can bid for a minimum of 110 equity shares and in multiples of 110 shares thereafter. At the upper end of the price band, retail investors will need to invest Rs 14,960 to apply for one lot, subject to applicable investor-category allocation rules.The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on November 25, while the company's shares are tentatively scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on November 27, 2026.SBI Capital Markets Limited, Axis Capital Limited, BOB Capital Markets Limited, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities Limited and IIFL Capital Services Limited are the book-running lead managers to the issue. KFin Technologies Limited is the registrar.The grey market premium (GMP) for Mahanadi Coalfields IPO is indicated at around Rs 3 per share, or nearly 2.2% over the upper price band of Rs 136. At this premium, the implied listing price works out to approximately Rs 139 per share. However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee the listing price or actual returns.About Mahanadi CoalfieldsIncorporated in April 1992, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Limited and is India's largest coal producer.The company primarily operates in the mining and production of non-coking coal across Odisha's Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields. articles.title: Gold plunges 3% to one-year low as hawkish Fed lifts dollar, yields
articles.summary: Gold plunged to its lowest level in more than a year on Wednesday as hawkish Federal Reserve signals strengthened expectations of further interest-rate increases, lifting the dollar and Treasury yields, Bloomberg News reported.Spot gold fell 3% to $3,736.06 an ounce at 11:43 a.m. ET after touching $3,734.76 earlier in the session, its lowest level since September 26, 2025. US gold futures for December delivery dropped 3.2% to $3,739 an ounce.The metal fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025 and was heading for a third consecutive session of losses.“We believe the selloff reflects mounting pressure from a strengthening US dollar, rising Treasury yields and expectations of further monetary tightening. Yesterday’s economic figures reinforced this sentiment,” Naeem Aslam, chief investment officer at Zaye Capital Markets, told Reuters.The dollar rose to a fresh 19-month high as hawkish remarks from Fed officials and recent economic data reinforced expectations of an interest-rate increase next month.For live updates on US Markets, click hereFed Governor Christopher Waller said Wednesday that the central bank needed to respond more aggressively to inflation by either raising rates by half a percentage point in December or signalling a faster pace of increases in 2027.New York Fed President John Williams said Tuesday that the central bank still had work to do to return inflation to its 2% target. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said the economy would probably require “several interest-rate increases” before spring.Markets see a 92% probability of a 25-basis-point increase in December and an 8% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool. They are also pricing in quarter-point increases in January and by April.Expectations of tighter policy have pushed the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield toward its longest stretch above 5% in nearly two decades. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding non-interest-bearing assets such as gold.The stronger dollar also makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.“It is a tough environment for gold, particularly with buying interest still subdued,” said Christopher Wong, a strategist at Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp, to Bloomberg. He said the market would remain cautious without a clear catalyst for a reversal.Gold has lost more than a quarter of its value since the US-Iran war began in late February. The conflict has pushed energy prices higher, fueled inflation and prompted central banks to tighten monetary policy.Investors are now awaiting minutes from the Fed’s October 27-28 meeting for further clues about the rate path. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh avoided directly addressing monetary policy earlier this week, consistent with his stated preference not to provide near-term rate guidance.“If the minutes reinforce concerns about persistent inflation and support additional tightening, Treasury yields and the dollar could strengthen further, potentially extending gold’s decline below $3,800,” Aslam added.Other precious metals also fell sharply. Spot silver declined 5.3% to $44.88 an ounce after touching its lowest level since September 26, 2025.Platinum dropped 4.6% to $1,363.50 after hitting its lowest level since September 17, 2025, extending its year-to-date loss to 33%. Palladium fell 2.6% to $945.95, its lowest level since early November.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

India's gold imports in the current fiscal could decline to USD 40 billion, down from about USD 72 billion in FY26, as the duty hike has helped slow inbound shipments, a top official said on Wednesday.

In May, the government had hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent, from 6 per cent, to contain non-essential imports.
India imported USD 71.98 billion gold in FY26, up from USD 58.01 billion in FY25.
Gold imports declined about 40 per cent to USD 24.78 billion during April-October this year, from about USD 41.24 billion in the corresponding period in 2025.
